detail.text: Forester on the 22nd. Snow free both sides, the chute is dry, Tyndall Creek is ankle deep. August walking. The only conditions note is smoke drifting in from the west in the afternoons.

detail.author: trailname_Yardsale

extraction.quote_span: one 30 foot snow patch, no axe no spikes

detail.quote: one 30 foot snow patch, no axe no spikes
detail.text: Forester 7/2 at 6am, chute is dirt and rock steps now with one 30 foot snow patch, no axe no spikes. Kearsarge exit same day, cruiser. Tyndall knee deep in the morning. The freeze last night was solid, everything firm before 8.

detail.author: u/postholepete

extraction.quote_span: Boot pack all the way up the chute, firm at 5am, axe in hand but never needed it, spikes did the work

detail.quote: Boot pack all the way up the chute, firm at 5am, axe in hand but never needed it, spikes did the work
detail.text: Came back for Forester 6/14 after our May bail. Night and day. Boot pack all the way up the chute, firm at 5am, axe in hand but never needed it, spikes did the work. Over the top by 7. Tyndall at dawn was knee high. Patience wins in a big snow year.

detail.author: trailname_Gears
detail.text: Forester 6/13 NOBO. Chute had a solid boot pack, axe out for maybe 10 minutes, no big deal. Snow starts around 12,000 on the south side. Tyndall crossing thigh high at 5pm, do it in the morning. Second year on trail, this is way more snow than 2022.

detail.quote: Tyndall was dangerous at midday, waist deep and fast
detail.text: Attempted Forester 5/26. Deep snow from Tyndall on, navigation entirely on GPS, the chute had no boot pack and we did not like the runout so we turned around and camped. Crampons and axes and we still bailed. The couple behind us kept going, hope they are ok. Tyndall was dangerous at midday, waist deep and fast.
